components.title: App bar
jobs: Material Design 3 Expressive app bars: small, medium flexible, large flexible, and search, from the HTML.
useWhen: Page title and screen-level actions.
avoidWhen: Peer destinations need navigation; categories need tabs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Small, medium flexible, large flexible, and search app bars.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native header/nav composition; AppBar owns scroll collapse and search expansion.
limitations: Native zoom, screen-reader announcements, contrast themes and physical mobile keyboard behavior remain pending manual review.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Choose small, flexible medium/large or search app bars for the title and screen actions. Preserve meaningful headings, named actions and reachable controls through scrolling and collapse.

materialGuidance.reason: Google replaces baseline medium/large bars with flexible variants. ExpressiveCSS medium and large already mean medium-flexible and large-flexible; keep those classes.

components.selectionExample: A Home/Search/Profile row belongs in navigation, even if placed at the top. Keep the app bar for the title and screen actions.

gaps.description: Native zoom, screen-reader announcements, contrast themes and physical mobile keyboard behavior remain pending manual review.
gaps.nextStep: Run the App bar/search fixture in the accessibility manual-review checklist with the actual devices and assistive technology.

browserChecks.name: AppBar native search dismissal and reopening (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Native Escape, canceled Escape, close-button, form and programmatic dismissal; focus-before-close ordering, fresh focus and pointer reopening, retained query, nested/referenced views and both motion preferences. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run in the same suite.

browserChecks.name: AppBar focus ownership and teardown (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Application close-handler focus, disabled fields, two app bars, non-dialog views, observer/listener teardown and remount without duplicate opening.

browserChecks.name: AppBar collapsed actions remain reachable (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Medium/large sticky headers at 320px with translated enlarged headings, keyboard focus through real scroll collapse, LTR/RTL, both motion preferences and reachable unobscured actions. Not native zoom.

components.title: Navigation bar
jobs: Switch between UI views on compact and medium screens.
useWhen: Persistent peer destinations on compact screens.
avoidWhen: Commands need buttons; local panels need tabs.

adaptive.reason: Use persistent peer navigation at wider widths.

implementation.documentedSupport: Stacked and horizontal destination layouts.
implementation.webAdaptation: Links navigate; the application marks the current destination.

upstreamReview.note: Rendered prose reviewed; collapsed token tables, image-only measurements, runtime and full parity unverified. See the design priority component review for requirement-level findings.

materialGuidance.reason: Google replaces the baseline bar with the flexible bar. The documented stacked/horizontal navigation-bar layouts remain current; do not exclude the family by its name.

components.selectionExample: Overview/Activity within an account page should not displace Home/Search/Profile in app navigation. Use tabs for those local panels and preserve the app destinations across widths.

components.title: Navigation rail
jobs: Switch between UI views on mid-sized devices.
useWhen: Collapsed, expanded, or modal peer navigation; the Expressive drawer replacement.
avoidWhen: Compact peers fit a navigation bar; verify nesting support.

adaptive.reason: Compact peer destinations fit the bottom edge.
Use the expanded rail when labels should remain visible.

implementation.documentedSupport: Collapsed, expanded, and modal rails.
implementation.webAdaptation: The compact expanded rail uses a scrim and dismissal behavior.

upstreamReview.note: Rendered prose reviewed; collapsed token tables, image-only measurements, runtime and full parity unverified. See the design priority component review for requirement-level findings.

materialGuidance.reason: Google replaces the baseline rail with the collapsed rail and the drawer with the expanded rail. The documented collapsed, expanded and modal variants remain current. Retain a drawer only for compatibility, an explicit request or a verified target-version nesting gap.

browserChecks.name: partial replacement and client navigation preserve shell ownership across repeated mounts
browserChecks.scope: Rail shell ownership; enhanced select interaction; generated Menu registry/resource cleanup; tooltip ownership across route replacement.

components.title: Panes
jobs: Material 3 canonical layouts, from the HTML.
useWhen: Responsive list-detail or supporting layouts.
avoidWhen: A single collection needs a list, not multiple panes.

adaptive.reason: Stack or collapse panes when their container cannot preserve useful pane widths.

implementation.documentedSupport: List-detail, supporting pane, and equal panes.
implementation.webAdaptation: CSS viewport and container queries; the application chooses the active compact pane.
limitations: Compact supporting layouts retain one-active-pane selection rather than automatic stacking. Native zoom, assistive technology and physical-device review remain pending.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
sections: Canonical examples/List-detail and Supporting pane/Across breakpoints
upstreamReview.requirements: List-detail uses one pane on compact windows, usually one on medium and two on expanded windows. Supporting content stacks below primary content on compact and medium windows, then sits alongside it on expanded windows. Preserve selection and scroll state.

materialGuidance.reason: Canonical layout pattern, not a standalone component.

components.selectionExample: A contact directory with no detail view needs a list. Use list-detail panes when selecting a contact reveals a separate detail region.

gaps.description: Compact supporting layouts retain one-active-pane selection rather than automatic stacking. Native zoom, assistive technology and physical-device review remain pending.
gaps.nextStep: Keep selection application-owned and complete the Panes manual-review fixture before making accessibility-parity claims.

browserChecks.name: complete list-detail example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only compact/detail switching, focus return, read state, breakpoint resizing and themed treatments.

browserChecks.name: Panes use the nearest available width at layout boundaries (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Independent viewport/container widths, both sides and exact 840px/1200px boundaries, nearest-container precedence, viewport fallback, pane aliases, start/left supporting columns, equal/three-pane, separated/floating and RTL. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run in the same suite.

browserChecks.name: Panes preserve footer icon-button geometry (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: All five icon-button sizes retain their height, width and block padding for native buttons and anchors across footer aliases. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run in the same suite.

browserChecks.name: Panes preserve compact selection and independent scrolling (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Active selection and first-pane fallback through resizing, independent body scrolling, DOM order, translated footer actions at enlarged root text size, both directions and motion preferences. Not native zoom or screen-reader verification.

components.title: Footer
jobs: Site navigation and extra information at the end of a page.
useWhen: Site links and legal information at page end.
avoidWhen: Primary app destinations need persistent navigation.

implementation.documentedSupport: Native footer with navigation columns and copyright content.
implementation.webAdaptation: Web page landmark styled with theme roles.
limitations: A document-level contentinfo landmark is checked; section-scoped footers and responsive legal links remain unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use a document footer landmark where appropriate, name distinct navigation groups and preserve meaningful links, reading order and reflow.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: Home/Search/Profile should not require scrolling to a footer. Use a navigation bar or rail for those destinations.

gaps.description: A document-level contentinfo landmark is checked; section-scoped footers and responsive legal links remain unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Place a document footer outside main and sectioning elements; verify named legal navigation at enlarged text.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining web navigation, badges and list controls expose their meaning
browserChecks.scope: Named navigation, document footer, unavailable pagination non-link, named badge count, list checkbox and scoped TOC aria-current. No spoken-output assertion.

components.title: Tabs
jobs: Material Design 3 tabs, from the HTML.
useWhen: Switch related content panels within one page.
avoidWhen: App destinations need navigation; values need inputs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Primary and secondary tabs; stacked and horizontal icon layouts.
implementation.webAdaptation: Links target panels; use the shipped runtime keyboard contract.
limitations: Native links use Tab and aria-current; runtime does not implement composite tab arrow keys.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference inputs-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use primary or secondary tabs for related content, with consistent labels and icons, selected state and reachable overflow. Google describes arrow navigation; native anchor navigation is a distinct web adaptation.

components.selectionExample: Home/Search/Profile are app destinations, so use a navigation bar or rail. Overview/Activity panels within one account page can use tabs; Day/Week/Month as a form value can use native radio inputs.

gaps.description: Native links use Tab and aria-current; runtime does not implement composite tab arrow keys.
gaps.nextStep: Retain native anchor semantics. Rendered selection, overflow geometry and teardown are covered; verify spoken current-state output and physical touch manually.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining suggestions and section links preserve selection and dismissal
browserChecks.scope: Native section links, retained search query and single-select suggestions, Arrow/Enter/Escape/Tab; no spoken-result assertion.

browserChecks.name: Tabs synchronize swipe selection and callbacks (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: LTR/RTL and ordinary/reduced motion selection state and single callbacks.

browserChecks.name: Tabs restore panels on teardown and remount (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Panel order, owned styles and semantics, wrapper cleanup and remount.

browserChecks.name: Tabs threshold keeps native links and ordinary panels (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Above-threshold ordinary panels, native Tab/Enter, disabled and external-target links.

browserChecks.name: Tabs hash selection, native dragging and overflow geometry (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Initial hash overrides stale authored panel state without initialization callbacks and restores it on teardown; actual pointer dragging, RTL overflow indicator geometry and initialization-only threshold; no physical touch or native zoom claim.

components.title: Breadcrumbs
jobs: The path to this page, from the HTML.
useWhen: Ancestor path to the current page.
avoidWhen: Peer views need tabs; numbered results need pagination.

implementation.documentedSupport: Breadcrumb links and app-bar composition.
implementation.webAdaptation: Labelled navigation with an ordered list and current-page link.
limitations: Named navigation and current-page markup are checked; CSS separator speech and long-path reflow remain unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use named hierarchy navigation with real ancestor links and a current-page state. It communicates location, not peer categories.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: Overview/Activity/Billing are peers, not ancestors. Use tabs for their same-page panels, not a breadcrumb trail.

gaps.description: Named navigation and current-page markup are checked; CSS separator speech and long-path reflow remain unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Inspect assistive-technology output for separators and test translated paths without truncating essential context.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining web navigation, badges and list controls expose their meaning
browserChecks.scope: Named navigation, document footer, unavailable pagination non-link, named badge count, list checkbox and scoped TOC aria-current. No spoken-output assertion.

components.title: Pagination
jobs: A list of pages. The HTML is the component.
useWhen: Move through pages of one result set.
avoidWhen: In-page sections need anchors or scrollspy.

implementation.documentedSupport: Page links, active page, and unavailable previous/next items.
implementation.webAdaptation: CSS-only navigation; the application supplies destinations.
limitations: aria-disabled and pointer-events alone cannot disable a link for keyboard users.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Name result-page navigation and previous/next actions. Expose the current page and make unavailable actions genuinely unavailable to keyboard users.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: A long article with Introduction/Methods/Results needs section links, optionally with scrollspy, not numbered result pages.

gaps.description: aria-disabled and pointer-events alone cannot disable a link for keyboard users.
gaps.nextStep: Use a non-link unavailable control, verify actual page destinations and preserve current-page state after updates.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining web navigation, badges and list controls expose their meaning
browserChecks.scope: Named navigation, document footer, unavailable pagination non-link, named badge count, list checkbox and scoped TOC aria-current. No spoken-output assertion.

components.title: Menu
jobs: Material Design 3 menus, from the HTML.
useWhen: Material Design 3 menus, from the HTML.
avoidWhen: The choices need persistent layout space, blocking interaction, or peer navigation.

implementation.documentedSupport: Vertical menus, nested flyouts, grouping, and standard/vibrant styles.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native menu/li structure; Menu owns opening and keyboard behavior.
limitations: Closing focus exclusion, scoped nested keys, RTL flyout placement and representative item targets have browser checks. Spoken output and full visual parity remain unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference inputs-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Choose the current standard, vibrant or grouped menu for a set of choices. Verify 48dp actionable targets, unclipped placement, first-item focus, arrows, typeahead, Escape and submenu navigation. A menu item should not contain multiple independent controls.

gaps.description: Closing focus exclusion, scoped nested keys, RTL flyout placement and representative item targets have browser checks. Spoken output and full visual parity remain unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Review spoken nested-menu context, translated labels and visual parity in the target application.

browserChecks.name: partial replacement and client navigation preserve shell ownership across repeated mounts
browserChecks.scope: Rail shell ownership; enhanced select interaction; generated Menu registry/resource cleanup; tooltip ownership across route replacement.

browserChecks.name: resource observations detect omitted teardown after a partial replacement
browserChecks.scope: Negative control proves resources remain without destroy; no visual parity assertion.

browserChecks.name: Menu cancels superseded callbacks and teardown work (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Open/close reversal and destruction during opening/closing preserve visibility, focus and completion callback ownership. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run in the same file.

browserChecks.name: Menu excludes closing content and preserves callback focus (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Tab exclusion during nonzero closing transitions, callback-directed focus, reopening, autoFocus false, and authored inert restoration. Ordinary and reduced motion; equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run in the same file.

browserChecks.name: Menu scopes nested keys and mirrors flyouts in RTL (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Nested entry/return keys, innermost Escape, scoped typeahead, disabled activation, representative 44px targets, single activation, and both viewport edges in LTR/RTL. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run in the same file.

browserChecks.name: Menu consumers keep values and focus through closing (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Enhanced select submits the selected value and changes once; autocomplete selection retains input focus; Tab skips closing lists. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run in the same file.

components.title: Scrollspy
jobs: Highlight the table of contents as the page scrolls.
useWhen: Track visible sections in a table of contents.
avoidWhen: Separate views need navigation or tabs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Section tracking and table-of-contents links.
implementation.webAdaptation: Web document navigation helper.
limitations: A scoped TOC current link is checked; shared observer behavior with different offsets and multiple independent TOCs remains unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use named in-page navigation, real fragment links, stable heading IDs and current-section state. Account for sticky offsets and reduced-motion preferences.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: A settings screen with mutually exclusive panels needs tabs. Scrollspy only tracks sections already present in the scrolling document.

gaps.description: A scoped TOC current link is checked; shared observer behavior with different offsets and multiple independent TOCs remains unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Use getActiveElement to select the correct TOC; test independent offsets and teardown before claiming multi-TOC support.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining web navigation, badges and list controls expose their meaning
browserChecks.scope: Named navigation, document footer, unavailable pagination non-link, named badge count, list checkbox and scoped TOC aria-current. No spoken-output assertion.

components.title: Buttons
jobs: Material Design 3 common buttons, icon buttons, and FABs — from the HTML.
useWhen: Run an action with a visible label.
avoidWhen: Stored choices need inputs; destinations need links.

implementation.documentedSupport: Filled, tonal, outlined, elevated, and text; xsmall through xlarge.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native buttons run commands; a.button links navigate.
limitations: Standalone common buttons do not document a square/toggle shape-morph contract; do not borrow icon-button or connected-group modifiers.

upstreamReview.note: Rendered prose reviewed; collapsed token tables, image-only measurements, runtime and full parity unverified. See the design priority component review for requirement-level findings.

materialGuidance.reason: Google no longer recommends 24dp padding for small buttons; use the current 16dp inset. This is spacing guidance, not removal of a button style.

components.selectionExample: Use radios for saved form values; buttons run commands.

gaps.description: Standalone common buttons do not document a square/toggle shape-morph contract; do not borrow icon-button or connected-group modifiers.
gaps.nextStep: Define and test a standalone shape-morph contract without borrowing connected-group or icon-button modifiers.

browserChecks.name: complete settings example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only responsive layout, targets, keyboard settings and save behavior, themed treatments; no component-wide parity.

browserChecks.name: complete editor example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only input, group toggle, preview/focus, save and bfcache-style remount behavior, themed treatments.

browserChecks.name: complete list-detail example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only compact/detail switching, focus return, read state, breakpoint resizing and themed treatments.

components.title: Icon buttons
jobs: A single icon as the whole control, in four styles and five sizes.
useWhen: Compact actions with recognizable icons.
avoidWhen: An unfamiliar action needs a visible button label.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard, filled, tonal, outlined; five sizes; narrow, wide, and square.
implementation.webAdaptation: Accessible name belongs to the control; the glyph is decorative.
limitations: Elevated and text are not icon-button variants.
Existing group checks cover selected icon colors and press shapes, not all standalone target sizes and disabled states.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
sections: Overview/M3 Expressive update: replacement guidance; Specs/Baseline tokens
upstreamReview.requirements: Distinguish default and toggle controls, sizes, shapes and widths. Name each action and expose toggle state. Verify 48dp effective targets even for visually smaller sizes, and sufficient icon contrast.

materialGuidance.reason: Google deprecates baseline filled, tonal and outlined token sets in favor of updated tokens, not those current icon-button variants. Do not rename framework tokens from Android examples.

components.selectionExample: A novel approval workflow should use a labeled button. A tooltip on an ambiguous icon cannot replace a clear label or the control's accessible name.

gaps.description: Existing group checks cover selected icon colors and press shapes, not all standalone target sizes and disabled states.
gaps.nextStep: Measure XS/S effective targets and test named default/toggle controls outside groups.

browserChecks.name: button-group toggle colors resolve in a browser
browserChecks.scope: Filled icon button selected color and glyph fill inside a button group only.

browserChecks.name: keyboard press changes icon widths and rendered corners
browserChecks.scope: Icon children inside button group only.

components.title: Button groups
jobs: Related action or toggle buttons that grow and reshape together, in two variants and five sizes.
useWhen: Cluster commands or aria-pressed toggle buttons.
avoidWhen: Submitted values need segmented or other native inputs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and connected groups; commands and opt-in selection.
implementation.webAdaptation: Runtime coordinates neighboring widths and selection; CSS handles connected shapes.
limitations: Existing geometry and keyboard checks do not cover every required-selection and overflow configuration.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Choose standard or connected groups and optional, required, single or multiple selection deliberately. Verify press growth, shapes, 48dp targets and reachable unwrapped content. Google describes Tab between buttons, with no focus on the group itself.

materialGuidance.reason: Google recommends the connected button group instead of segmented buttons. Match toggle state, required selection and persistence explicitly; native form submission is not supplied by aria-pressed.

components.selectionExample: Standard groups fit Cut/Copy/Paste commands; connected groups fit toggle choices. A pressed button does not submit a radio value: use native inputs for form values, or explicitly integrate persistence.

gaps.description: Existing geometry and keyboard checks do not cover every required-selection and overflow configuration.
gaps.nextStep: Exercise empty optional and required selection, disabled neighbors and constrained translated labels.

browserChecks.name: button-group toggle colors resolve in a browser
browserChecks.scope: Rendered group behavior; does not establish standalone common/icon-button parity.

browserChecks.name: button-group geometry resolves for overrides, targets, and RTL
browserChecks.scope: Rendered group behavior; does not establish standalone common/icon-button parity.

browserChecks.scope: Rendered group behavior; does not establish standalone common/icon-button parity.

browserChecks.scope: Rendered group behavior; does not establish standalone common/icon-button parity.

browserChecks.scope: Example-only input, group toggle, preview/focus, save and bfcache-style remount behavior, themed treatments.

components.title: Split button
jobs: A lead action and a trailing half that opens a menu of related ones, in five sizes.
useWhen: Default action plus related menu actions.
avoidWhen: Equal actions need a group; values need inputs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Leading action and trailing menu trigger with matching styles.
implementation.webAdaptation: Reuses Menu; no separate split-button runtime.
limitations: Full leading-action versus trailing-menu activation and Escape return are not directly mapped.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Keep the leading default action distinct from the trailing additional-choices menu. Name both controls, expose the trailing expanded state, return focus after dismissal and verify separate 48dp effective targets.

components.selectionExample: PDF/CSV format selection for a later Export action belongs in a select or native inputs. A split button fits Export now plus alternate export commands.

gaps.description: Full leading-action versus trailing-menu activation and Escape return are not directly mapped.
gaps.nextStep: Activate both halves with keyboard and pointer; verify expanded state and separate effective targets.

components.title: Floating action button
jobs: One primary action or a FAB menu of related labelled actions.
useWhen: One primary action or a FAB menu of related labelled actions.
Replace removed speed dials with fab-menu and labelled actions.
avoidWhen: The action is not the single highest-priority screen action.

adaptive.reason: Use the extended FAB when the action benefits from a visible label.

implementation.documentedSupport: FAB sizes, extended FABs, and menus of related actions.
implementation.webAdaptation: Floating action behavior uses the documented FAB runtime.
limitations: Full visual parity and spoken assistive-technology output remain unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use one primary, non-destructive action. Current guidance discourages the small FAB. Extended FABs have visible labels; FAB menus contain two to six labelled actions and must not hide focused controls.

materialGuidance.reason: Google no longer recommends small FABs, baseline extended FABs or surface-colored FABs. The 40dp FAB and sizeless extend variant are removed. Use circle extra for the 56dp FAB, or its medium and large sizes. Extended FABs require extend small, extend medium or extend large; the small extended FAB remains recommended. Use primary/secondary/tertiary container roles instead of surface colors. Use fab-menu for labelled related actions; speed-dial APIs are removed.

gaps.description: Full visual parity and spoken assistive-technology output remain unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Review rendered variants and spoken labels before claiming full parity.

browserChecks.name: FAB menu preserves keyboard, dismissal and responsive behavior
browserChecks.scope: Click state, hover inactivity, Tab, Escape, action activation, outside focus, reinitialization, reduced motion and narrow layout.

browserChecks.name: current FAB sizes preserve geometry and explicit extended variants
browserChecks.scope: Chromium: button and link FAB geometry, explicit extended sizes and label roles in light/dark themes; baseline extended styling is absent.

components.selectionExample: Speed dials have been removed. Replace legacy fab or fixed-action-btn wrappers with fab-menu and labelled actions; use a toolbar for persistent commands.

components.selectionExample: A hundred compact activity records need a list. Giving every row a card adds separation without a separate content or action group.

gaps.description: Existing card lifecycle and geometry evidence does not cover every selected variant, contrast and reflow state.
gaps.nextStep: Measure and keyboard-test the chosen variant with long content and nested controls.

browserChecks.scope: Chromium: zero and 1.2s container timing, reopening, cancellation, native close, removal, destruction and focus return. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run separately in the browser suite.

components.title: Dialogs
jobs: Important prompts in a user flow. Dedicated to a single task.
useWhen: Focused prompts or decisions that interrupt the flow.
avoidWhen: Ignorable feedback needs snackbar or inline feedback.

implementation.documentedSupport: Basic and full-screen dialogs.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native dialog.showModal()/close(); shared dialog behavior is separate from AutoInit.

upstreamReview.note: Rendered prose reviewed; collapsed token tables, image-only measurements, runtime and full parity unverified. See the design priority component review for requirement-level findings.

components.selectionExample: Saving successfully should not force dismissal of a dialog. Use a snackbar for that feedback and inline feedback for a persistent nonblocking issue; reserve a confirmation dialog for a decision that must precede the action.

components.title: Bottom sheet
jobs: Secondary content anchored to the bottom of the screen.
useWhen: Secondary content anchored to the bottom of the screen.
avoidWhen: Persistent wider-window secondary content or a small anchored choice fits another component.

adaptive.reason: Persistent secondary content fits beside the main task.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and modal bottom sheets.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native dialog.show()/showModal(); shared runtime handles dragging and dismissal.
limitations: The shared handle dismisses rather than cycling sheet heights; long-content and drag behavior are outside the new modal check.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Distinguish standard and modal sheets. Keep overflowing content scrollable, close actions reachable and height changes available without dragging. Verify the selected width and margin configuration against Google measurements.

gaps.description: The shared handle dismisses rather than cycling sheet heights. Interrupted-drag cleanup has rendered coverage; bottom-sheet long-content and physical-touch review remain pending.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining sheet variants retain native modal focus and explicit close actions
